title: SLA breach response: emergency fleet controls and autoscaler rollback plan
creator: Nina Kaur
description: Summary: On 2026-03-04 18:10 UTC the Dedicated fleet experienced a throughput shortfall causing an SLA breach for reserved customers. Symptoms: elevated queueing on gateway, higher 95th/99th token latencies, and automatic routing to lower-tier model variants. Immediate cause: a mis-deployed autoscaler config removed the rapid-burst scaling rule and reduced target utilization from 70% to 40% for certain pools. Contributing factors: lack of synthetic traffic checks in the deploy pipeline, an alert that suppressed paged notifications during weekends, and insufficient preflight validation of autoscaler rules against canary traffic patterns.
notes: This ticket tracks the response and post-incident actions specific to Dedicated throughput guarantees and fleet controls rather than the broader root-cause engineering investigation (see linked postmortem). Aim is to codify emergency runbook steps, short-term mitigations, and prioritized durable fixes to prevent recurrence and meet SLA commitments.
timeline:
2026-03-04 17:58 UTC - Autoscaler config promoted from staging to prod via infra-deploy pipeline.
2026-03-04 18:10 UTC - Gateway queue depth spikes observed by telemetry; alert fired (non-paged).
2026-03-04 18:22 UTC - First customer complaint (support ticket).
2026-03-04 18:30 UTC - On-call notified via Slack after escalation; Diego takes lead.
2026-03-04 18:45 UTC - Manual scaling of affected pools to +40% capacity performed; immediate latency improvement.
2026-03-04 19:15 UTC - Autoscaler config rolled back to previous commit; canary validated; gradual normalization by 19:40 UTC.
immediate_actions_taken: 1) Manual override: increased pool desired counts by 40% for pools A/B/C. 2) Rolled back autoscaler policy to commit b2f4d3 within 35 minutes of detection. 3) Enabled paged alerting for critical capacity alerts and set temporary on-call handoff. 4) Notified impacted customers with status updates and compensation plan options.
root_cause_conclusion: Mis-deployment of autoscaler rules removed burst scaling and lowered utilization target. The deploy lacked a synthetic load preflight and the alerting pathway had a weekend suppression rule that prevented timely paging. The autoscaler itself behaved as configured; the configuration change was the primary fault.
action_items: AI-1: Add autoscaler config validation to CI - create integration test that simulates burst traffic (owner: Priya S.) due 2026-03-20
AI-2: Harden deploy pipeline to require preflight synthetic load checks for autoscaler changes (owner: Diego R.) due 2026-03-17
AI-3: Restore paged alerts for capacity-critical SLOs and add redundancy in on-call rotation (owner: Marcus Lee) due 2026-03-12
AI-4: Implement an emergency 'capacity-safety' policy that reserves a 20% buffer for reserved pools during config rollouts (owner: Aya Thompson) due 2026-04-01
AI-5: Add a post-deploy canary traffic monitor dashboard and automatic rollback trigger if queue depth increases >30% over baseline (owner: SRE team) due 2026-03-31
AI-6: Customer communications template and SLA remediation playbook for billing adjustments (owner: Olivia Park) due 2026-03-15
acceptance_criteria:
1) CI integration test exists and fails if autoscaler removes burst rule.
2) Deploys of autoscaler changes require green synthetic load preflight.
3) Capacity paged alerts are active with verified paging tests.
4) Emergency capacity-safety policy is enabled with telemetry verifying buffer is not consumed during normal ops.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Reserving a 20% capacity buffer increases cost; trade-off accepted short-term for SLA protection. Automatic rollback on canary failures may increase churn during noisy measurements; mitigation is to tune thresholds and require manual confirmation for low-confidence signals.
review_comments: Marcus Lee (SRE): Confirmed that manual scaling successfully reduced tail latencies — recommend keeping emergency scale runbook as a separate step in console.
Priya S. (Infra): Will add unit and integration tests for autoscaler rule schema; need API contract for burst-rule flags.
Asha Patel (PM): Prioritize customer-facing remediation and clear SLAs for compensation; schedule a customer all-call once root cause doc is published.
Diego Ramirez: Assigned to lead infra changes and immediate rollout of pager config; coordinating with SRE and Support.
Security (Jamal Reed): No secrets or KMS actions impacted; security review not required for these fixes.
customer_notifications: Sent initial status 2026-03-04 20:05 UTC via Support; follow-up remediation email scheduled for 2026-03-11 with credits offer and technical summary.
how_to_runbook: Emergency runbook added to docs: 1) Validate metrics (queue depth, token latency, utilization). 2) If autoscaler misconfig suspected: enable manual desired count, notify customers, rollback last autoscaler commit, and escalate to infra. 3) If capacity cannot be recovered within 60 minutes: activate cross-region routing to adjacent Dedicated pools or temporary hosted fallback per policy.
final_resolution_status: Remediated - autoscaler rollback and manual scale; durable fixes in progress
